Rating: 9/10

Elden Ring is an extraordinary gaming experience, and one that's difficult to put into words. Its world-building and level design are nothing short of outstanding. 

The map is massive and constantly subverts your expectations. Just when you think you've reached the end, it keeps expanding with new regions and massive underground areas. Every location feels distinct, and the art direction is phenomenal. The graphics are solid, too. I played this completely blind, exploring and clearing almost every corner of the map over 180 hours, and I was constantly mesmerized by just how beautiful the environments looked. It doesn't rely on heavily cinematic set pieces to impress you; the sheer scale and design of the world do that on their own. It's undoubtedly a game that will go down in gaming history.

The difficulty might seem intimidating at first, but the open-world design gives you plenty of freedom to tackle its challenges your own way. Whether it's experimenting with different weapons, trying out magic, or making use of Ashes of War, there's no shortage of ways to approach combat. Personally, I stuck to a single weapon and a shield, focusing on mastering the core melee combat with strength build. 

The bosses are mostly fantastic, with Malenia being an absolute standout. However, I do have one major complaint: the delayed attacks. Some bosses hold their swings for an absurdly long time, seemingly just to catch you mid-dodge. It feels more like an artificial way of increasing difficulty than a genuinely challenging attack pattern. Normal enemies also get a bit repetitive, but it never really bothered me.

Story-wise, it follows the classic FromSoftware formula. You're not spoon-fed the plot, but if you pay attention to the world, its characters, and the environmental clues, it's fairly easy to piece things together. The questlines are fun to figure out, although the clues about where to go next can sometimes be frustratingly vague. The deep lore is brought to life through excellent voice acting and an amazing soundtrack that perfectly complements the scale of the world. As for the ending, I understand and appreciate FromSoftware's minimalist approach to storytelling, so I wouldn't call it a major disappointment, but it did leave me wanting more. I save-scummed to experience all six endings, and getting a short cutscene felt like a bit of a letdown after investing 180 hours in such an incredible journey. 

Despite these minor complaints, the sheer freedom, beautiful art direction, and solid performance far outweigh the flaws. Whether you want to master a single weapon or replay the game ten times with ten different magic builds, there's plenty of room to experiment and enjoy yourself. Elden Ring lives up to the hype and is easily one of the best gaming experiences I've had. 

*Note: This review covers the base game only and does not include the DLC.*

Elden Ring is more than just a game; it's an unforgettable journey through a breathtaking world. Every corner of the Lands Between has something special to offer, from its stunning landscapes and mysterious ruins to its incredible atmosphere and hidden secrets.

The world feels alive with beauty, mystery, and danger. Exploring it is an experience unlike anything else. The art direction, world design, soundtrack, and attention to detail are simply outstanding. There are moments when you just stop playing, look around, and admire the beauty of the world FromSoftware has created.

What makes Elden Ring truly special is how it makes you feel like a small part of a vast, ancient world waiting to be discovered. Every journey, every discovery, and every challenge feels meaningful.

Thank you, FromSoftware, for creating such a masterpiece. Elden Ring is an experience I'll never forget, and one of those rare games that stays with you long after you've finished playing.

I started this game thinking, "Hmm... I don't think I'm good enough for a Souls game." Until one day, I said, NAY! I MUST! And thus, Elden Ring became not only my first FromSoftware game, but also my first ever Souls game.

Initially, I spent an embarrassingly long time trying to decide which starting class to pick. Then a friend suggested, "Let's go Wretch." And I thought, screw it. Let's go.

What followed was a rather interesting adventure of finding anything that moved, hitting it with a club, almost killing it, only for it to turn around and say, "Surprise MF!" Cue the words YOU DIED appearing on my screen so many times that they might as well have been permanently engraved into my soul.

But then, somewhere around level 20, I finally managed to kill that golden fella on the horse. And something clicked. That one victory kickstarted what would become one of, if not THE best gaming experiences I've ever had. The feeling of finding a boss, getting absolutely demolished, coming back for revenge, getting demolished AGAIN, and repeating that cycle until you finally land the killing blow...

Aaaaaah. Nothing beats it. The adrenaline rush, the satisfaction, the sheer disbelief when a boss that has been bullying you for the past two hours finally falls.

I came into this game wondering if I was good enough.

I left knowing that I was stubborn enough.

And honestly? I'd happily die another thousand times just to experience that first victory all over again.

elden ring was a game that took me an embarrassingly long time to get into, thanks to its overwhelmingly large world, the absurd difficulty of the bosses and enemies, and a complete lack of any exposition whatsoever. I had no motivation to push further into the game, to give it the time necessary to understand what made it special, and i regret not getting into it sooner. elden ring is one of the best games I've ever played, it uses a colossal open world and a completely hands-off approach to the player's exploration and development of strategies/builds to let you grow and take on its daunting obstacles and challenges by any means necessary.

i had assumed for the longest time that fromsoft games were just harsh challenges that asked the player to meet an uncompromising obstacle and tackle it exactly as it is, and to some extent thats true. bosses in elden ring have a fixed difficulty in the way that their health, attack patterns, and damage dealt cannot be changed, they exist as they are, and you have to find a way to defeat them. the change in difficulty instead comes from the player and your own progression, with complete freedom in what level you tackle the boss at, and what kind of items, spells, or spirit ashes you'll use for the fight you can almost always find a strategy to counter any boss, and a way to take an impossible fight and make it something manageable. i barely struggled any more than i needed to, and always found myself taking on bosses that i would be evenly matched with and able to reasonably beat (most bosses took maybe an hour tops, with the toughest taking multiple sessions but rarely more than maybe 4-5 hours total (except for the valiant gargoyles)). 

due to a lack of a strict narrative or proper exposition, the game allows the exploration to become the main point of the game, with whatever knowledge you gain as you wander forming your primary understanding of the world, letting the experience vary drastically from person to person. vague spoilers for the endings: [spoiler]it's only fitting that the choices you make and the endings of the game end up being heavily symbolic and vague, you wander a ruined and decaying world, so of course when it hits a breaking point, you get to decide what direction it goes into, whether to maintain the status quo with you on top, to simply burn it all down, or the most popular choice: to bring about a change so radical that the world will be unrecognizable from what it was before[/spoiler]. that exploration and deeply personal narrative and decision making allows for a level of investment and attachment that really make the game unforgettable. my first playthrough took a solid 160 hours and for the entire duration i was excited to keep pushing forward, the world stayed mysterious and dangerous and interesting, there is honestly nothing like it. i think its worth checking out. to say the least.

Stepping out of the Stranded Graveyard and into the blinding light of Limgrave for the first time is a moment burned into my brain. The game doesn’t hand you a mini-map cluttered with task markers, nor does it drag you through a two-hour tutorial on how to press buttons. It just places a towering, golden Tree Sentinel in front of you—who will promptly crush you into dust—and whispers, “Go figure it out.” That raw, uncompromising respect for the player's intelligence and curiosity is why I fell in love with Elden Ring. Exploration isn't a chore list; it’s genuine discovery. You see a colossal, decaying castle on the horizon or a faint purple glow down a random elevator shaft, and four hours later you’re deep underground in a subterranean starry night sky fighting a celestial ancestor spirit. Every victory feels earned, and every hidden ruin feels like a secret meant just for you.

What truly cements it as a masterpiece for me, though, is the unmatched depth of player freedom paired with FromSoftware's legendary lore and combat design. Whether you want to wield a colossal slab of iron, cast star-shattering gravity magic, or bleed your enemies dry with lightning-fast katanas, the game lets you define your own path to strength. When a boss like Radahn or Malenia pushes you to your absolute limits, it forces you to adapt, learn the cadence of their swings, and master the dance of combat. That cycle—going from getting completely obliterated to seamlessly dodging every strike and landing the final hit—delivers a rush of pure dopamine that very few other games can match. Woven through all of it is George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki’s tragic, haunting world of fractured gods and outer cosmos, turning every ruined church and obscure item description into a piece of a tragic puzzle. It’s relentless, unforgiving, and visually breathtaking—an unforgettable journey from Tarnished nobody to Elden Lord.

Elden Ring is bellow average overrated overhyped mediocrity that didn’t deserve GOTY 3.5/10

1. STORY 3/10 
Has interesting lore if you watch youtube videos but that is expected to be extra and not something you are obligated to do to understand the story, the story in game is for most part absent… that alone disqualifies the game from 10/10 even if everything else was perfect (everything else is indeed not perfect, actually not even close to 10), even when environmental story telling is used as an excuse, it still does very poor job at it, dark fantasy on its own doesn’t work once its removed from high fantasy setting where usually its just a small part of much bigger world… lord of the rings works because you can see the contrast… when you make the entire world look bleak it doesn’t make you feel anything anymore, and no it has nothing to do with morally ambiguous characters, i prefer those actually, what i don’t like is expecting me to feel something about a world that looks exactly the same… speaking of world

2. WORLD 2/10
Just straight up a chore, want to reach that lake? To bad you can’t glide so you have to go all the way around, fall in a ditch? To bad you can’t climb so you have to go all the way around… want to negate fall damage with the horse double jump? to bad you can’t… like im a missing something here or fromsoft still hasn’t discovered the most core mechanic of double jump… i get that jumping is alien tech to this guys so i guess that explains why it feels so bad, they copied the entire world from breath of the wild but didn’t bother copying the core traversal tools necessary to make the world enjoyable to traverse… other things such as all biomes just morphing into one made me lose complete track of time, everything looks the same (DLSS 5 is not the reason for that) there are so many reused enemies, assets and dungeons that doing any form of side content is not worth it… like its so bad that the map feels procedurally generated but somehow it was hand made? The world is nowhere near as big as people made it to be… 

pick a farm, milk it until you get as many runes as physically fast as possible for the shortest possible time and min max your character so you can finally do the “campaign” this is literally the entire progression system of the game, speaking of progression

3. PROGRESSION 0/10
Actually horrible, just straight up unplayable without external guide, going blind here would’ve made me uninstall and refund the game…. I never follow build guides for games and beat all the pinnacle bosses in poe 2 and not even once followed a build guides… but here its mandatory to even play the game… NPCs say bunch of nonsense… rarely if ever explain things and for most part ignored them or didn’t even find them…
No quest side window or markers means you have no idea what you are supposed to do, world and NPCs don’t make it any easier either…
Loot feels horrible which makes no sense for an ARPG, like thats literally the whole point of an ARPG… the loot… how do you screw this bad to the point that the only way to progress is to follow build guides and have to look the individual weapons, items and gear on a website map to find them… no side content such as cave or fortress felt rewarding… (all who were reused assets of course) 

4. UI/UX, CONTROLS, CAMERA 0/10
My gosh, the most horrific controls i have ever endured… probably second worse after crimson desert (Thank god didn’t buy that steaming pile of trash) everything is wanky and weird and the UI is atrocious… like there is no way there is no key for inventory… thats straight up disrespectful towards the player… it costs the devs nothing to do that and somehow its missing from the game… game is locked at 60fps and has no DLSS SR forcing me to use mods and also no mini-map, seriously? It doesn’t make the game more realistic or quirky… its annoying af, the whole UI is convoluted and just straight up horrible… even compared to old games its terrible… you know what else is terrible? Camera… can’t imagine that camera with all the AoE garbage in the DLC, good thing is i don’t even plan to find out (even tho i did bought the DLC) 

5. GRAPHICS 4/10
They are fine, but they are not as good as people make them, the lighting and skybox is over compensating for the otherwise bellow average mediocre graphics and man there are moments where the textures are so bad it looks like a ps3 game… its so bad that even DLSS 5 doesn’t know what to do with it so it turns it into a giant blob of liquid noise unlike anything I’ve seen before, sure could be a mod problem but toggling it off absolutely showed horrible textures in that spot that don’t match the resolution of the tiles or bricks nearby… creating inconsistent resolutions in the same room… the render distance is bad and the texture quality completely deteriorates on distance the moment you look in any view of the world that wasn’t intended to be used as advertising material (such as limgrave door view) 

6. MUSIC 3/10
 Aside from the limgrave one, main theme, tree sentinels one and malenia’s song, everything is boring, mid and forgettable… genuinely disappointing music…

7. PLATFORMING -10000/10
don’t ever include platforming section in your games ever again

8.  DUNGEONS 2/10
Repetitive, boring and short… same layout for most part… same style, same material… everything just blurs together, the difficulty of the game is extensively used to make the cleaning of this areas far slower to dilute the actual size and length of the dungeons (just like the rest of the game)… there a few that stand out like Stormveil Castle that are medium size but still tiny compared to Zelda standards… overall the dungeons are extremely disappointing and often the way the developers have designed the levels feels like they are making it on purpose unclear so you miss out on “big things”…

9. DIALOGUE, VOICE-LINES, BEHAVIOUR 3/10
I get that Japanese games always have goofy and corny voice lines in their games but elden ring setting and tone is supposed to be serious yet the moment a boss says something its always some non sensical goofy garbage, while the NPCs having those type of lines is sometimes fine, the bosses completely ruin the tone of the game, fromsoft has failed at the first step of making bosses if a boss doesn’t feel scary… and no its appearance is less then 10% of what makes a boss scary, its behaviour and how they speak as well as their ambition is the primarily factor… it feels like fromsoft doesn’t know what it wants elden ring to be, do you want the world to feel cruel and unjust? Then why no encounter ever feels personal? 

10. CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP 0/10
Boring, repetitive and unfun, there is no point of killing any of the enemies because they will just respawn every time you go on a bonfire leading to feeling like you are not doing any form of progress, why bother with them if you can optimise for specific farm and only do that instead? And for the items you need you will just follow build guide so you know where to go and how to get what you need… bosses are same story… keep repeating the same thing over and over again until you finally beat it or over level your self so much that you demolish it… no fun middle ground… everything feels like artificial way of increasing the playtime and length of the game.

Never played a Fromsoft game before, and although I'm having fun, there are some issues I'm not seeing people talk about that I think should be mentioned. From most to least frustrating:
1. Consumables are awful. I hated them in Silksong, and I hate them here. I propose that they should not be permanently removed from your inventory after death unless you've made some permanent progress (beating a boss, touching a grace, etc.).
2. Abysmal keyboard controls. I've found a setup that works for me, but it's still very problematic. If I could bind multiple keys to the same action, or access the quick items without holding the interact button, it would be much better.
3. The 60 fps cap is stupid. Modders have fixed this issue. I've gotten used to it, but Fromsoft has no excuse.
4. Last, least, and most confusing, why is there no option for glyphs to automatically switch based on whether you're using a keyboard or controller? I also own a Legion Go, so if I want the glyphs to be accurate, I have to change a setting AND THE SETTING IS SYNCED BETWEEN DEVICES????

Overall, I like Elden Ring, and I'm interested to try Fromsofts other games, but these issues do not inspire confidence.

Best game ever.

While its not the absolute "perfect" video game imo, it combines most of the best aspects of ds1-ds3, layering it over an utterly massive open world that actually rewards you for exploring rather than just being a checklist of go here do that. While you can absolutely full clear everything you can technically beat the game in as little as 9 bosses. The community might frown on using everything you acquire in the game to win but dont let that stop you from summoning or using spirit ashes for a boss - elden ring is designed to let you play it how you want to, just know it wont pull any punches if you decide to limit yourself to 1v1 every boss because of pride. Overall great game and the dlc is just as densely packed with content and further encourages the explore everything mindset, arguably far moreso than the base game as it basically has its own separate leveling system.
